newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: McConnell Dowell aware of buyout talk.
newsitem.headline: McConnell Dowell aware of buyout talk.

text.p: McConnell Dowell Corp Ltd, a construction firm with operations in Australia and New Zealand, said on Friday that a dissident shareholder group at its parent firm planned to privatise the Australasian subsidiary.

"It has been brought to the board's attention that a North American group operating as the 'Committee to Revitalise Dominion Bridge Corp' (our 63 percent shareholder), has released a press announcement in New York to the effect that if successful in gaining management control of Dominion Bridge it would, as part of a three point strategy, then seek to privatise McConnell Dowell Corp Ltd," the company said.
"The company has had no contact with this group and can offer no further comment at this juncture," the company said.
Dominion Bridge shareholders will vote on July 18 on a motion by the dissident group to oust senior management.
A U.S. court also ruled against the company this week after it sought expedited hearings against the group, which it has charged with misrepresentations and a number of other commercial claims.
Dominion Bridge's 63 percent stake in McConnell Dowell, which has won a number of contracts in Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and Central Asia, is valued at A$78.58 million.
McConnell Dowell shares were steady at A$3.00 on Friday, giving the company a market capitalisation of A$124.72 million based on its 41.57 million shares outstanding.
Dominion Bridge, which is listed on NASDAQ, is an engineering firm based in Toronto.
The dissident group said on May 24 that it wanted to remove senior management which it held responsible for sharply lower profits and the falling share price.

The group said on July 2 that it would propose to buy the minority shareholding in McConnell Dowell to help consolidate and strengthen Dominion's cash flow and to make capital raisings Dominion reduced its stake in McConnell Dowell from 77.42 percent in March this year with a share placement to institutions in an attempt to improve liquidity in the local stock.
